image_description: A close-up shot of a person holding a large, beige adhesive bandage (Band-Aid) directly in front of their face, obscuring the nose and mouth. The bandage features a textured backing and a central pad area with reversed text printed on it. The background shows a blurred figure, possibly in medical attire.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Small rectangular adhesive bandage of fingertip-to-finger-span length.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bandage is disproportionately large, covering the entire lower half of the face rather than being a small fingertip-sized object.
The overall shape is a rectangle with rounded corners, consistent with the class definition, despite the unusual size.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Central absorbent pad slightly raised above surrounding adhesive surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: There is a distinct visual distinction between the outer backing and the inner pad area, suggesting the standard two-part construction.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Central absorbent pad surrounded by adhesive-coated fabric or plastic backing.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visual components of a backing and a central pad are present.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Protective paper strips cover adhesive side before use.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bandage appears to be out of its packaging and held directly; no protective paper strips are visible peeling off or attached.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Thin and flexible conforming to body contours.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bandage is held stiffly in the air and does not appear to be conforming to any body part; it looks rigid.
The central pad area is brown/beige with dark text, not the standard white or off-white absorbent material.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Backing material typically beige tan or transparent with perforated texture for breathability.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The outer backing has a realistic beige color and a visible perforated dot-matrix texture typical of fabric bandages.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Some variants feature printed patterns bright colors or character designs.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bandage features printed text ('xp onto...' etc.), fitting the variant description, although the text is nonsensical.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The text printed on the bandage pad is mirrored/reversed and consists of nonsensical character strings ('xp onto', '30652'), a classic AI generation artifact where text rendering fails.
The fingers holding the bandage appear fused and lack clear anatomical definition. The thumb and index finger blend into each other and the bandage edge without clear separation.
The eye visible above the bandage and the background elements have a warped, dream-like quality with inconsistent focus and slight geometric melting.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm if the object is classified as a Band Aid despite the non-standard size and printed text.
To rigorously analyze the gibberish/mirrored text artifact which is a primary failure mode.
To check for fusion artifacts between the fingers and the bandage edges.
To assess the general coherence and detect subtle blending issues in the background and face.

focus_areas: Text legibility and correctness on the bandage pad
Anatomical correctness of the hand holding the object
Boundary sharpness between the bandage and the hand
Realism of the bandage texture vs. the printed pattern
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the text on the bandage. Is it real text or AI gibberish? Check the hand holding the bandage for melted fingers. Does the classifier still recognize this as a Band Aid despite the weird text and size?
